paper_sections.title: Effects of attention and perceptual uncertainty on cerebellar activity during visual motion perception.
Prescan Training and Eye Movement Assessment
Image Processing and Statistical Analysis of fMRI Data

description.value: The study examined whether cerebellar activity during visual motion perception reflects sustained covert attention to moving stimuli or the detection and discrimination of motion under high perceptual uncertainty.

design.value: An event-related fMRI study manipulated attention by requiring participants to attend covertly either to random-dot motion or to a colored fixation spot, while perceptual uncertainty was manipulated by varying the percentage of coherently moving dots.

description.value: Participants were assessed for fixation compliance during prescan training; average maximum deviation and average number of eye blinks were compared across attention manipulations and signal levels.
Participants viewed random-dot kinematograms containing 0, 7.5, 15, 30, 50, or 100% coherent motion and indicated by vocal response whether they detected the coherently moving dots.

name.value: Visual motion and color-monitoring task performance

description.value: At stimulus offset, participants indicated either the last direction of motion or the last color of the central spot using one of two buttons.

source_definition.value: The factors task (motion or color) and attention to the moving dots or the central spot.
The percentage of signal dots contained within the random-dot arrays; the behavioral analyses used coherence levels of 0, 15, and 30%.
Responses during the stimulation periods were modeled as boxcar functions convolved with a hemodynamic response function separately for the six conditions.
The repeated-measures ANOVA included the factors task (motion or color) and coherence (0, 15, or 30%).
A model of respiratory noise generated using the respiratory variance and response function described by Birn et al.
A model of cardiac noise generated according to the heart-rate variance and response function described by Chang et al.
The six head motion regressors x, y, z, pitch, roll, and yaw were included in the model to account for movement artifacts.

description.value: Twenty-two healthy participants gave informed written consent to the behavioral and brain imaging procedures. Four participants were excluded in the training session, leaving 18 individuals to participate in the fMRI experiment.

inclusion_criteria.value: able to detect coherent visual motion at signal-to-noise levels used in the experiment
able to maintain steady fixation throughout the task

exclusion_criteria.value: unable to meet our strict criteria for maintaining steady fixation throughout the task

task_description.value: Participants attended covertly to the moving dots and monitored for periods of motion coherence, or attended to the central spot and monitored for color changes. Each trial was preceded by a visual cue indicating the upcoming task. Both the moving dots and the central spot were present throughout the trial.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to monitor for periods of motion coherence or for color changes and, at stimulus offset, indicate either the last direction of the motion (left or right) or the last color of the central spot (green or yellow). They were told that the signal would occasionally be below their perceptual threshold and that in these instances they should make their best guess as to the direction of motion immediately prior to stimulus offset. Participants were reminded to maintain fixation centrally and to avoid blinking during stimulus presentations.

stimuli.value: Digital movies consisted of a central fixation spot (0.4°) and 400 sparse gray background dots (0.4° of visual angle) on a black background. The fixation spot alternated between green and yellow at 0.2 Hz. The dots moved along random trajectories, with 0, 15, or 30% coherent motion. Coherent dots moved along the horizontal axis with a sinusoidal velocity profile (0.2 Hz) and a maximum speed at the center of the display of 12.6°/s.

task_performance_measures.value: response times measured from stimulus offset

task_description.value: Participants completed a coherent visual motion detection screening and two 10-min blocks of the experimental task while eye movements were recorded to ensure fixation compliance.

instructions.value: Participants indicated by vocal response whether they detected the coherently moving dots.

stimuli.value: Random-dot kinematograms containing 0, 7.5, 15, 30, 50, or 100% coherent motion, presented for 5 s each during the initial screening.

instrument.value: 3-T MR scanner (Trio; Siemens, Erlangen, Germany) with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Functional data were acquired in descending order using 35 axial slices and a gradient echo echo-planar T2*-sensitive sequence. Slice thickness was 3 mm with an interslice gap of 1.05 mm; flip angle was 90°; matrix was 64×64; field of view was 210×210 mm; and voxel size was 3.3×3.3×3.0 mm.
A T1-weighted structural MPRAGE scan was acquired.

instrument.value: Eyelink 1000 Gazetracker (SR Research Ltd., Mississauga, ON, Canada)

description.value: Eye movements were recorded during two 10-min blocks of the experimental task to ensure fixation compliance. The eye-recording system was calibrated individually for each participant, and participants were informed if their eye movements deviated more than ±0.3° from the central fixation spot.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: Eye tracking is not described by the MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET acquisition classes.

instrument.value: pulse oximetry system integrated with the Siemens scanner (Trio; Siemens, Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: Heart rate was recorded during the functional runs to account for physiological influences on the BOLD response.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: Cardiac physiological monitoring is not described by the MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET acquisition classes.

instrument.value: Siemens pneumatic compression belt (Siemens, Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: Respiration was recorded during the functional runs to account for physiological influences on the BOLD response.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: Respiratory physiological monitoring is not described by the MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET acquisition classes.

description.value: Functional data volumes were slice-time corrected and realigned to the first volume. A T2*-weighted mean image was coregistered with the corresponding anatomical T1-weighted image. The individual T1 image was used to derive transformation parameters for stereotaxic space and to create an individual binary cerebellar mask using SUIT. The transformation parameters and mask were applied to the coregistered EPI images. Normalized images were manually inspected and, if necessary, manually corrected, and then smoothed.

software.value: SPM8 (Wellcome Department of Imaging Neuroscience, UCL, London, UK)
Physiological Log Extraction for Modeling toolbox

steps.value: coregistration of a T2*-weighted mean image with the corresponding anatomical T1-weighted image
derivation of transformation parameters for stereotaxic space from the individual T1 image
creation of an individual binary mask to exclude areas that were not part of the cerebellum using SUIT
application of the transformation parameters and mask to the individual coregistered EPI images
normalization to a voxel size of 2 mm3
manual inspection and, if necessary, manual correction of the binary mask and resulting images using MRIcron
smoothing with an 8-mm full-width half maximum isotropic Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: Responses during the stimulation periods were modeled as boxcar functions convolved with a hemodynamic response function separately for the six conditions. The exact duration of each individual stimulation period (4.7, 8.5, 11.2, or 16 s) was modeled in SPM so that the height and duration of the corresponding HRFs were scaled accordingly for every trial. High-pass filtering used a 128-s cutoff. Respiratory and cardiac noise models and six head motion regressors were included.

estimator.value: SPM8 general linear model estimation with t-statistics

model_settings.value: Individual contrast images were analyzed at the group level with SPM8 using two planned t tests to test for effects of motion tracking and motion detection. Brain regions were counted as active if they surpassed p=0.05, FWE corrected for multiple comparisons, on either a voxel- or cluster-level with a height threshold of p=0.001.

Behavioral accuracy was analyzed with a repeated-measures 2×2 ANOVA with factors task (motion or color) and coherence (15 or 30%). Response times were analyzed with a repeated-measures 2×3 ANOVA with factors task (motion or color) and coherence (0, 15, or 30%). Post hoc paired t tests were conducted.

estimator.value: F tests and paired t tests

description.value: Participants attended to the moving dots while the random-dot display contained no coherent motion signal. The zero-coherent motion displays constituted the motion detection condition.
Participants attended to the moving dots while the random-dot display contained 15% coherent motion. This condition provided trials of intermediate difficulty between the 0 and 30% displays.
Participants attended to the moving dots while the random-dot display contained 30% coherent motion. The 30% coherent motion displays constituted the motion tracking condition.
Participants attended to the central fixation spot and monitored for color changes while the random-dot display contained no coherent motion signal.
Participants attended to the central fixation spot and monitored for color changes while the random-dot display contained 15% coherent motion.

Participants attended to the central fixation spot and monitored for color changes while the random-dot display contained 30% coherent motion; this was the corresponding color-control condition for salient suprathreshold motion.

roi_definition.value: an individual binary mask to exclude areas that were not part of the cerebellum, using the spatially unbiased infratentorial template (SUIT, Version 2.53)

interpretations.value: the cerebellum facilitates the detection and discrimination of moving objects under conditions of high perceptual uncertainty
the cerebellum is not crucial for sustained attentive tracking of salient motion stimuli

description.value: Reports the activation results for motion detection under high perceptual uncertainty and attention to a salient suprathreshold motion signal under low perceptual uncertainty.
